learningObjective: Diagnose register-spill-induced slowdown from Nsight Compute metrics and compiler diagnostics.

canonicalClaims.claim: Register spilling is diagnosed via non-zero stack frame + spill stores/loads in ptxas -v output and confirmed by abnormally high L1 local-load traffic in Nsight Compute; mitigations reduce register pressure through __launch_bounds__, -maxrregcount, refactoring, or algorithmic changes.
conditions: ptxas output shows non-zero stack frame and spill stores/loads.
Kernel is compute-tail-bound with Long Scoreboard stalls.
nonImplications: Does not imply all spills are fatal.

misconceptions.claim: Shared memory and register file are the same resource.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They are separate hardware resources on the SM.

misconceptions.claim: Higher blockDim reduces per-thread register pressure.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-thread register usage is determined at compile time by the kernel code, not by launch configuration.
This env var controls host-side blocking behavior of API calls.

misconceptions.claim: Local memory in CUDA is on-chip.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Despite the name, CUDA local memory is backed by device DRAM (with L1/L2 caching).
